chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you slaughter a slaughtered animal and find a complete foetus in its belly, then eat (it); and if it does not happen to be complete, then do not eat (it).

key_terms.الذَّبِيحَة: The slaughtered animal — the validly slaughtered beast whose internal contents are under discussion
key_terms.تَامّ: Complete/fully formed — the critical legal criterion for permissibility; a foetus with complete hair, hooves, and features
key_terms.وَلَد: Offspring/foetus — here refers to an unborn animal found inside the womb

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating a foetus found inside a slaughtered animal?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a jurisprudential ruling on the permissibility of consuming a foetus found inside a freshly slaughtered animal. The ruling is conditional on the foetus being fully formed (taamm): if complete, it is permissible to eat; if incomplete, it must not be consumed. This ruling reflects classical Islamic fiqh principles where the slaughter of the mother confers ritual permissibility to a fully developed foetus found within.
